headline: Broad Rally Lifts August's Opening Session as Diplomacy Fuels Risk Appetite
body_html:
Wall Street kicked off August with a decidedly bullish tone on Monday, as optimism surrounding ongoing Iran nuclear negotiations gave investors a fresh reason to rotate into cyclicals and growth names alike. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by nearly three to one across our 519-name universe — 388 stocks finishing higher against just 131 in the red — a breadth reading that points to broad-based conviction rather than a narrow index lift.

Materials and Industrials led all sectors, gaining 2.35% and 2.29% respectively, with Homebuilders and Consumer names not far behind. The rotation away from defensives was crisp: Energy was the lone sector in negative territory, slipping 0.41% even as OPEC+ output decisions lingered in the background. Semiconductors lagged the broader tape with a gain of less than 1%, suggesting some residual caution in high-multiple hardware names.

The session's standout mover was Hims & Hers Health, which surged nearly 11% to top the gainer board — a notable outperformance even within an otherwise strong Healthcare group. First Solar and SolarEdge each climbed more than 9%, making solar the day's most electrified sub-theme. On the downside, TG Therapeutics shed more than 11%, the sharpest single-stock loss of the day, a reminder that idiosyncratic risk never fully takes a holiday.

briefs.headline: Iran Diplomacy Tone Sets the Table for Risk Rally
briefs.body: Investors leaned into risk assets after reports emerged that the United States and Iran are engaged in active deal negotiations, with Washington issuing pointed warnings about the consequences of failure. The diplomatic backdrop gave equity markets a constructive macro narrative to open the month, helping lift cyclicals and rate-sensitive sectors broadly.

briefs.headline: Boeing Shares Surge on Convergence of Positive Catalysts
briefs.body: Aerospace giant Boeing saw its shares soar Monday after three separate favorable developments emerged simultaneously, sending the stock sharply higher. The move provided a meaningful lift to the Industrials sector, which finished as the second-best performer of the session with a gain of 2.29%.

briefs.headline: Visa Moves to Fortify Fraud Defenses With $2.4 Billion Acquisition
briefs.body: Payments heavyweight Visa announced an agreement to acquire identity-intelligence firm BioCatch for $2.4 billion, citing a rapid escalation in AI-driven fraud schemes as the strategic rationale. The deal signals that major financial networks are willing to deploy significant capital to stay ahead of increasingly sophisticated cyber threats.

briefs.headline: Solar Names Ignite as First Solar and SolarEdge Climb Past 9%
briefs.body: First Solar and SolarEdge each surged more than 9% on Monday, making solar the most energized sub-sector of the session. The twin moves came against a backdrop of broader risk-on sentiment and added momentum to a Homebuilders-and-industrials-led cyclical rotation that defined the day's character.

briefs.headline: UBS Hit With $125 Million Fine Over Money-Laundering Lapses
briefs.body: Swiss banking giant UBS agreed to pay $125 million to U.S. regulators to resolve money-laundering violations, according to reports. The penalty adds to a growing list of compliance-related settlements across the financial sector and underscores continued regulatory scrutiny of large international institutions operating in American markets.

briefs.headline: TG Therapeutics Leads Decliners With Double-Digit Drop
briefs.body: TG Therapeutics fell more than 11% on Monday, making it the steepest single-session loser in our universe and a sharp outlier on an otherwise strongly positive tape. AstraZeneca and Indivior also weighed on the Healthcare-Pharma group, which managed only a modest overall gain despite the broader market's bullish tone.
